title: Lapse-Day Credit Conventions for Late-Renewed Rental Property Service Contracts
content:
**Lapse days.** The lapse days of a late renewal of a Rental Property Service Contracts contract are the calendar days after the expired term's end date and before the late renewal date.

**Credit rule.** The lapse-day credit follows why the contract lapsed:

1. When the renewal notice for the expired term was issued fewer than the tier's renewal-notice days (45 on every tier) before the term end and automatic renewal was on, the adjusted premium is multiplied by 365 less the lapse days and divided by 365.
2. When the notice was issued that late and automatic renewal was off, the adjusted premium is multiplied by 52 less the whole weeks of lapse and divided by 52. The whole weeks are the lapse days divided by 7, counted down to a whole number.
3. Otherwise no lapse credit is given and the adjusted premium stands for the full year.

The adjusted premium is the late-renewal premium after its adjustment rate and before rounding. The late-renewal premium after the lapse-day credit is rounded to the cent once at the end.

**Records read.** The renewal notice date, the term end date and the automatic renewal setting of the expired term, on the contract.

## Combinations

| Notice issued fewer than 45 days before the term end | Automatic renewal | Lapse-day credit |
|---|---|---|
| yes | on | multiply by 365 less the lapse days, divide by 365 |
| yes | off | multiply by 52 less the whole weeks of lapse, divide by 52 |
| no (45 days or more before) | on or off | none |

## Hypothetical late renewals (adjusted premium $700.00)

- Term ended 30 June, renewed on 11 July: the lapse days are 1 to 10 July, 10 days. Notice 40 days before the term end, automatic renewal on: $700.00 times 355 divided by 365 is $680.82 after rounding.
- Same dates, automatic renewal off: 10 days is 1 whole week; $700.00 times 51 divided by 52 is $686.54 after rounding.
- Notice exactly 45 days before the term end: no lapse credit, $700.00.
